14 This matter came before the Honorable Alberto E. Tolentino on May 29, 2026, for a
15
Further Proceedings. Defendant Philip J. Cruz ("Defendant") was present with counsel Public
16
Defender Ramiro Orozco. Assistant Attorney General Vernon Hosannah was present for the
17
People of Guam ("People"). Following the hearing, the court took the Defendant's Motion to
18
19 Withdraw as Counsel under advisement pursuant to Supreme Court of Guam Administrative Rule
20
06-001, CVR 7.l(e)(6)(A) and CRl.l of the Local Rules of the Superior Court of Guam. Having
21
duly considered the parties' briefings, oral arguments, and the applicable law, the court DENIED
22
the Defendant's Motion to Withdraw as Counsel, and now issues this Decision and Order
23
memorializing its previous ruling.
24
25 BACKGROUND
26
Based on events that occurred on or about September 22, 2020, the Defendant was charged
27
with the following offenses: (1) BURGLARY (As a 2nd Degree Felony); (2) ATTEMPTED
28
Decision & Order Re. Motion to Withdraw as Counsel

Page I of6

THEFT (As a 2nd Degree Felony); and (3) CRIMINAL MISCHIEF (As a Misdemeanor). See
Indictment (Aug. 26, 2021 ). The Public Defender Service Corporation ("Public Defender") was
2
3 appointed as counsel for the Defendant on August 14, 2021. See Notice (Aug. 14, 2021).
4
While jury selection and trial was originally set for May 4, 2022, the court rescheduled
5
jury selection and trial for June 2, 2026, in light of several warrants for the Defendant's arrest led
6
and the recent assertion of his right to speedy trial in April of this year. 1 The Defendant
7
subsequently filed two motions on May 5, 2026: (1) Defendant's Motion in Limine to Exclude
8
9 Prior Bad Acts Evidence; and (2) Defendant's Motion to Compel Disclosure of Witness
10
Information and for Sanctions. On May 12, 2026, the Defendant filed two more motions: (1)
11
Defendant's Motion to Dismiss for Prosecutorial Misconduct; and (2) Motion to Withdraw as
12
Counsel ("Motion to Withdraw"). Upon filing this Motion to Withdraw, the Defendant filed a
13
14 Motion to Compel the Government to Provide Offer of Proof Regarding Availability of Ivy
15
Austria. The People also filed its Non-Opposition to the Motion to Withdraw.
16
At a Motion Hearing, the court addressed the parties' arguments on several motions,
17
including the Motion to Withdraw. See Mot. Hr'g Mins. at 2:26:27PM (June 1, 2026). Having
18
considered the parties arguments and applicable law, the court denied the Motion to Withdraw
19
20 for reasons set forth below. Id.
21
DISCUSSION
22
A. Although the Public Defender's Motion to Withdraw was filed without leave of court,
23 the court has an obligation to consider the merits of the motion before rendering its
decision.
24
Before addressing the substance of the Motion to Withdraw, it is noteworthy that the
25
26 Defendant's Motion to Withdraw was filed beyond the court's deadline of May 5, 2026. See
27
1 See Criminal Trial Scheduling Order (Oct. 29, 2021); see also Bench Warrant (Oct. 12, 2022); see also Bench
28 Warrant (Dec. 20, 2025); see also Bench Warrant (Nov. 24, 2025); see also Criminal Trial Scheduling Order (Apr.
10, 2026); see also Assertion (Apr. 7, 2026).
Decision & Order Re. Motion to Withdraw as Counsel

Page 2 of6

Criminal Trial Scheduling Order (Apr. 10, 2026). If a motion is untimely filed, the court may
allow the filing of motions beyond the time limit previously set by the court. See 8 GCA § 65 .45
2
3 ("Failure by a party to raise defenses or objections or to make requests which must be made prior
4
to trial, at the time set by the court pursuant to § 65 .15, or prior to any extension thereof made by
5
the court, shall constitute a waiver thereof, but the court for cause shown may grant relief from
6
the waiver.").
7
8 "Papers required to be served shall be filed with the court. Papers shall be filed in the
9 manner provided in civil actions." 8 GCA § 1.29(d ). "Papers not timely filed by a party including
10
any memoranda or other papers required to be filed under this Rule shall not be considered
11
without leave of court." CVR 7.l(f). The scope of the Civil Rules of the Local Rules of the
12
Superior Court of Guam does not extend to criminal matters unless they are inconsistent with
13
14 rules that apply. See CVR 1.1. In this case, the Defendant through counsel was not granted leave
15
of court to file any of his motions that were filed beyond May 5, 2026.
16
Public Defender argues that "[t]he timing of this conflict is directly attributable to the
17
Government's delayed disclosure of information relating to Ms. Sablan." Def.'s Mot. Withdraw
18
(May 12, 2026). Despite asking for discovery from the People since September 10, 2021, Public
19
20 Defender notes that it had not requested information related to Naomi Bermudes Sablan
21
specifically until May 4, 2026; almost two weeks after the parties' deadline to exchange mutual
22
discovery and file motions to compel lapsed. Although the People filed its witness list on May 5,
23
2026, her name was included in the Affidavit of Probable Cause attached to the Magistrate's
24
25 Complaint filed on August 14, 2021. See Magistrate's Compl., Aff. (Aug. 14, 2021).
26
Counsels are reminded of its obligation to "act with reasonable diligence and promptness
27
in representing a client" pursuant Guam Rule of Professional Conduct ("GRPC") 1.3. Despite the
28
Decision & Order Re. Motion to Withdraw as Counsel
People v. Cruz, CF0397-21
Page 3 of6

failure to timely file a Motion to Withdraw in this case, the court still has an obligation to analyze
the merits of the issue before it.2
2
3 B. The Public Defender has not shown that its representation of Defendant Cruz will
result in a violation of its obligations to Ms. Naomi Sablan as a former client under
4
GRPC 1.9.
5
When filing motions in criminal matters, the Local Rules of the Superior Court of Guam
6
reads as follows:
7
(1) Required Pleadings. An application to the court for an order shall be by
8
motion. A motion other than one made during a trial or hearing shall be in
writing unless the court permits it to be made orally. It shall state the grounds
9
upon which it is made and shall set forth the relief or order sought. It shall be
10 supported by a memorandum containing citations of authority and may also
be supported by affidavit. The motion shall also include copies of all
11
documentary evidence that the moving party intends to submit in support of
12 the motion. Additionally, all motions and each response or opposition thereto
shall contain a statement whether an evidentiary hearing is requested and an
13 estimate of the time required for the presentation of the evidence and/or
arguments. The reply brief shall contain a re-estimate of the time or a statement
14
that the original estimate is unchanged.
15
CR l.l(b)(l) (emphasis added). Although Public Defender's memorandum contains no citations
16
of authority for the court to consider regarding an attorney's material limitations by
17
responsibilities to former clients and a duty of confidentiality, the court will review the issue of
18
19 the Public Defender's withdrawal pursuant to GRPC 1.16 and 1.9.
20
GRPC 1.16 states in relevant part that "a lawyer shall not represent a client or, where
21
representation has commenced, shall withdraw from the representation of a client if the
22
representation will result in violation of the rules of professional conduct or other law." Guam R.
23
Profl Conduct l.16(a)(l). Here, Public Defender requests its withdrawal as counsel for the
24
25 Defendant due to its previous representations in other closed criminal cases of Naomi Bermudes
26
27 2 In Petition ofQ uitugua v. Flores, the Supreme Court of Guam held that "the failure to file a written opposition, the
filing of a notice non-opposition, or the disregard of untimely filed papers" does not relieve the lower court of its
28
obligation to consider the merits of a motion before rendering its decision. Petition ofQ uitugua v. Flores, 2004 Guam
19 ,r,r 27-28.
Decision & Order Re. Motion to Withdraw as Counsel
People v. Cruz, CF0397-21
Page4 of6

Sablan; one of the People's potential witnesses. As the governing authority for an attorney's
withdrawal due to conflicts of interest with former clients, GRPC 1.9 states the following:
2
3 a. A lawyer who, has formerly represented a client in a matter shall not
thereafter represent another person in the same or a substantially related
4
matter in which that person's interests are materially adverse to the
interests of the former client unless the former client gives informed
5
consent, confirmed in writing.
6 b. A lawyer shall not knowingly represent a person in the same or a
substantially related matter in which a firm with which the lawyer formerly
7
was associated had previously represented a client
8 1. whose interests are materially adverse to that person; and
11. about whom the lawyer had acquired information protected by
9 Rules 1.6 and 1.9(c ) that is material to the matter; unless the former
client gives informed consent, confirmed in writing.
10
c. A lawyer who has formerly represented a client in a matter or whose
11 present or former firm has formerly represented a client in a matter shall
not thereafter:
12
1. use information relating to the representation to the disadvantage
of the former client except as these Rules would permit or require
13
with respect to a client, or when the information has become
14 generally known; or
11. reveal information relating to the representation except as these
15
Rules would permit or require with respect to a client.
16
Guam R. Profl Conduct 1.9. At a continued Pre-Trial Conference, the People represented to the
17
court that it had no intent on calling the witness at issue within the Motion to Withdraw. See Pre
18
Trial Conference Mins. at 2:43:07PM (May 29, 2026). Upon that representation, Public Defender
19
indicated that a conflict no longer is present. Finding that the Public Defender's representation of
20
21 the Defendant will not result in violation of GRPC 1.9, the court denies the Defendant's Motion
22
to Withdraw as Counsel at this time.

For reasons stated above, the court hereby DENIES the Defendant's Motion to Withdraw
